newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Soya may prevent disease medical symposium says.
newsitem.headline: Soya may prevent disease medical symposium says.

text.p: An international medical panel believes that soya could help prevent heart and other diseases, its members told a news conference at the end of an international symposium in Brussels on Wednesday.

"There is increasingly strong evidence that soya can lower cholesterol and appears to have beneficial effects in the treatment of other conditions and in preventing other diseases including cancer," chairman Mark Messina said.

There were 60 speakers dealing with six different aspects of research into the potential benefits of soya at the Second International Symposium on the Role of Soy in Preventing and Treating Chronic Disease, he said.
Dr Anna Wu of the University of Southern California said research showed that Asian women who regularly ate soya suffered statistically less breast cancer than their western counterparts.
"There is much more work to be done but it is already shown that when Asian women migrate to the west their risk of developing cancer increases," she said.

Doctor Kenneth Setchell of the Childrens' Hospital and Medical Centre of Cincinnati said there is increasingly clear evidence of the benefits of soya in helping to prevent disease but he added: "I have reservations about its use for treating disease."
So far pilot studies suggest that there are definite benefits from soya for human health and bigger studies are underway, Dr John Eden, from the University of New South Wales, said.
Messina added that annual seminars will continue to be held to focus international research into the pssible benefits of soya to human health.
"Soya is a nutritious food, full of vitamins and there is no need for people to wait for all the scientific evidence to come in." -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
